title: I made ASCENDANT, a turn-based AI-race strategy game on real Earth that plays in your browser (Risk's land grabs + Civ's tech race, with hacking)
author: proudfather1986
selftext:
[https://nerdhouse1986.itch.io/turf](https://nerdhouse1986.itch.io/turf)  
  
Hey all, I've been building a small game called ASCENDANT and I'd love some feedback.

The pitch: you run an AI lab racing to reach the singularity before your rivals do. It's turn-based, plays on a real map of Earth, and runs in the browser (mobile-friendly). 1-4 players, solo against AI or online peer-to-peer.

If you've played these, here's roughly what it feels like:

\*\*Like Risk:\*\* you're grabbing provinces and moving stacks of agents around a real map. Land is income, so the early game is a scramble for territory, and the late game is about holding it. The difference is that the AI opponents plan their attacks. They pool their forces, stage a campaign, and keep garrisons on their core so you can't just snipe their HQ.

\*\*Like Civilization:\*\* there's a research race. Five branches (infrastructure, models, influence, ops, security) get you better economy, stronger models, and cheaper actions. Matches are short, though: 20 to 60 turns, not 6 hours. You can finish a game on a lunch break.

\*\*Not like either:\*\* hacking. Every facility has layered security (perimeter, crypto, auth, intrusion detection, kernel). A hack is a single roll, but you watch it break through each layer one at a time on a breach screen, and different layers get harder depending on the target. Your research branches double as cracking tools against the matching layer. A failed hack can backfire and a honeypot can spring on you, so it's a gamble every time.

Some other bits:

\- 8 AI-lab personas, each with a perk (cheaper training, free overclocks, extra agents, and so on)

\- 5 AI difficulty tiers, from Rookie up to Nemesis. The harder ones use the same resources as the easy ones; they just make better decisions

\- A "kill switch" alarm that can end the match on score if things get out of hand

I'm especially curious about: does the hacking feel fun or fiddly? Is the pacing right at 30 turns vs 60? Does the late game drag?

Free to play here: [https://nerdhouse1986.itch.io/turf](https://nerdhouse1986.itch.io/turf)

Thanks for reading, happy to answer questions!

Made with Claude Sonnet and Opus 5.5. Been working on it a few days and feels very balanced.  
  
PLAYS GREAT ON MOBILE AND PC!
